# PageRank

*Metric* · also written BackRub

Google's original link-based ranking algorithm, from the BackRub research project at Stanford.

**Glossary** (*PageRank and BackRub*): PageRank is the link-analysis algorithm Google's founders invented; BackRub was their 1995 Stanford search engine, soon renamed Google. Google's ranking systems guide says PageRank has evolved and is still part of its core ranking systems.

8 claims mention it: 2 from Google's documentation, 5 shown or said at the event (2 not in Google docs, 1 confirmed by Google docs, 2 consistent with Google docs), 1 the author's analysis. A card is a map: cite the claim ids, with the citation given after each claim.

## Google's documentation

Documented in: [A guide to Google Search ranking systems](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/ranking-systems-guide), [From the garage to the Googleplex](https://about.google/our-story/).

- [`D3-C138`](../sessions/D3-S05-how-google-thinks-about-quality.md) Docs: Google's ranking systems guide says PageRank, one of its core ranking systems when Google first launched, has evolved a lot since then and continues to be part of its core ranking systems. `[D3-C138, docs, Google Search Central, https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/ranking-systems-guide]`
- [`D3-C233`](../sessions/D3-S07-what-are-quality-updates.md) Docs: Google's company history page says the Google story began in 1995 at Stanford, where Larry Page and Sergey Brin built a search engine that used links to judge the importance of pages, called it Backrub and soon renamed it Google; Google Inc. was founded in August 1998. `[D3-C233, docs, Google, https://about.google/our-story/]`

## Shown or said at the event

Not in Google's documentation first: present those as said at Search Central Live, never as documented policy.

- [`D3-C136`](../sessions/D3-S05-how-google-thinks-about-quality.md) Stage, Day 3, not in Google docs: Google's quality talk called PageRank the speaker's favourite ranking system, elegant in its time, but said Google does not really use it so much anymore. `[D3-C136, stage, Google, Day 3]`
- [`D3-C251`](../sessions/D3-S07-what-are-quality-updates.md) Stage, Day 3, not in Google docs: In the mid-1990s the web was small enough to list in one manually edited directory; by the time BackRub was being built, directories could no longer find information on the growing web, which is why Google was created. `[D3-C251, stage, Google, Day 3]`
- [`D3-C133`](../sessions/D3-S05-how-google-thinks-about-quality.md) Slide, Day 3, confirmed by Google docs: Google's slide said there is not one single ranking system and named spam detection systems, the reviews system, BERT, MUM, RankBrain, freshness systems, deduplication systems, crisis information systems and link analysis systems (PageRank). `[D3-C133, slide, Google, Day 3]`
- [`D3-C231`](../sessions/D3-S07-what-are-quality-updates.md) Stage, Day 3, consistent with Google docs: Google began as a Stanford research project in 1995: Larry Page and Sergey Brin built a search engine on an algorithm they invented, PageRank, and called the engine BackRub. `[D3-C231, stage, Google, Day 3]`
- [`D3-C232`](../sessions/D3-S07-what-are-quality-updates.md) Stage, Day 3, consistent with Google docs: BackRub was renamed Google when it launched officially, which the speaker dated to 1997-98. `[D3-C232, stage, Google, Day 3]`

## The author's analysis

- [`D3-C137`](../sessions/D3-S05-how-google-thinks-about-quality.md) Analysis: The remark that PageRank is not used so much anymore differs from Google's ranking systems guide, which says PageRank has evolved a lot and continues to be part of the core ranking systems; read it as PageRank weighing less among many signals, not as PageRank being switched off, so links still matter. `[D3-C137, analysis, Ibrahim Anjro]`
